VALIDATION grep not literally empty: it still returns 3 andes45 matches in src/pipeview/kanata_pipeline.hpp lines 30/169/491 ('Port of Python ... from tools/andes45.py' / 'andes45 style'). These are historical port-attribution comments in KEPT C++ code; the file is byte-identical between base and qemu-isa-match, is not in v001's file scope, and qemu-isa-match ITSELF fails this same over-broad grep. I did not edit it (that would break the series' byte-identical invariant and exceed scope). All DELETED-artifact patterns return zero, so the validation's intent (no dangling refs to removed files) is satisfied. Side note: after deleting tools/andes45.py these 3 comments now reference a removed file as provenance.

I wrote the C++ --kanata wording from the real --kanata/--objdump options in src/main.cpp (added a 'Generating the Pipeline Log' section and changed the konata.py line to '--kanata log'). So the new series' PIPELINE.md intentionally differs from qemu-isa-match, consistent with it being an edited_only text fix.

Dockerfile:17 'python3-pybind11' apt package was left in place: it is now unused (pybind11.cpp is gone) but Dockerfile is not in v001's file scope, not in edited_only, is byte-identical to qemu-isa-match, and is outside the validation grep's --include set. Kept byte-identical; flagged as a follow-up cleanup candidate.

TDD: no RED test was written. v001 is a pure removal/structural-cleanup + doc rewrite of dead, never-compiled code (ENABLE_PYBIND11 never set), which changes no runtime behavior; the spec's own gate for v001 is the grep, and abi=none with no test files.
